classification.difficultyReason: Substantial transfer, coordinated cases or justification beyond a direct worked-example substitution. Page 51 demonstrates a three-set intersection of a union, with C above A and B; pages 49–50 establish the component operations.

inlines.text: Use a Venn diagram of three intersecting sets

answer.short: Both sides shade the parts of $A$ overlapping $B$ or $C$, including the triple intersection.
answer.worked: For $A\cap(B\cup C)$, retain the part of $B\cup C$ inside $A$. For $(A\cap B)\cup(A\cap C)$, combine the two overlaps with $A$. Both include exactly the same regions, including $A\cap B\cap C$.

spec.description: Paired three-circle diagrams with A lower left, B lower right and C above; shade A intersect B and A intersect C. No universal rectangle is needed for this three-set identity; labels and captions are outside the circle strokes.

answer.short: Both sides shade all of $A$ and the overlap $B\cap C$.
answer.worked: The left side includes all of $A$ together with $B\cap C$. On the right, all of $A$ lies in both unions. Outside $A$, a point lies in both unions only when it belongs to both $B$ and $C$. The shaded regions coincide.

spec.description: Paired three-circle diagrams shading all of A and the overlap of B with C. No universal rectangle is needed for this three-set identity; labels and captions are outside the circle strokes.
